findings.explanation: google_sql_database_instance.this sets encryption_key_name (CMEK). For Cloud SQL to actually use a customer-managed key, GCP requires the Cloud SQL service agent to hold roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on that exact key. Fixed by adding data.google_project.this and google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.cloudsql_sa in example/examplea/google_kms_key.sql.tf. Also promoted to a real deterministic policy (HLD_GCP_453) in the holden engine itself, including a core engine fix (followModuleVariable in resolveEdgeTarget) so the check resolves correctly across the module boundary.
findings.title: CMEK key referenced by encryption_key_name has no companion IAM binding granting the Cloud SQL service agent decrypt access

findings.explanation: The settings block repeats the exact same two-line { name = ..., value = ... } shape eight times for log_lock_waits, log_disconnections, log_connections, log_checkpoints, log_duration, log_hostname, log_statement, and cloudsql.enable_pgaudit. A rules engine scores single-resource complexity but has no similarity pass across sibling blocks within one resource, so it can't flag that a dynamic block over a local map/list would collapse this to one place, making it trivial to add or audit a flag later.
findings.title: Eight near-identical database_flags blocks could be a single dynamic block

findings.explanation: google_sql_database_instance.instance.tf now declares google_monitoring_alert_policy.this, added in this same review session to close the HLD_GCP_337 gap. The .pike/pike.generated_policy.tf custom role (README's documented 'Role and Permissions' least-privilege grant for whoever applies this module) lists only cloudsql.*, compute.*, servicenetworking.*, and resourcemanager.projects.get — no monitoring.* permission at all. A rules engine can't catch this: it requires knowing that a specific resource TYPE in one file implies a specific IAM permission STRING that should appear in an unrelated custom-role resource in another file, then confirming it's actually absent. Anyone who has locked their CI/Terraform service account down to exactly this generated role (the entire point of generating it) will get a permission-denied error applying this module now, not a security exposure, but a real functional break introduced by this session's own alert-policy fix.
findings.remediation:
Add the Monitoring Alert Policy CRUD permissions to the role (normally this file is regenerated by the pike pre-commit hook from actual resource usage — running that regenerates it correctly; the permissions below are the minimal manual equivalent):

  "monitoring.alertPolicies.create",
  "monitoring.alertPolicies.delete",
  "monitoring.alertPolicies.get",
  "monitoring.alertPolicies.list",
  "monitoring.alertPolicies.update",
  "monitoring.notificationChannels.get"
findings.title: Pike-generated least-privilege Terraform role is missing Monitoring API permissions for the alert policy this module now creates
